description: The i20 price page lists the base Era at ₹5,99,000 ex-showroom. Era uses the 1.2 l Kappa petrol with a 5-speed manual: 1,197 cc, 83 PS and 114.7 Nm.
Starting price is ₹10,99,200 ex-showroom. HX 2 is the entry trim and is offered with the 1.5 l MPi petrol and a 6-speed manual: 1,497 cc, 115 PS and 143.8 Nm.
The lowest listed ex-showroom price is the Z2 Petrol (E) 7-seater manual at ₹13,69,000. It uses the 2 L mStallion turbo petrol: 149.14 kW and 370 Nm, with a 6-speed manual.
Mahindra lists THAR OG from ₹10.32 lakh ex-showroom. AXT is the entry grade and is offered only with the 1,497 cc D117 CRDe diesel, 6-speed manual and rear-wheel drive: 87.2 kW and 300 Nm.
Bolero starts at ₹8.57 lakh ex-showroom. B4 is the first listed grade. The mHawk75 diesel is 1.5 L, 55.9 kW and 210 Nm, with a 5-speed manual, and the same engine is listed for B4, B6 and B6(O).

The lowest petrol ex-showroom row is Alto K10 Std (O) at ₹3,69,900. It is not an AGS variant. The model page states 65.7 bhp, 89 Nm, a 998 cc K10C petrol engine, and about 24.39 km/l for petrol manual variants.

Toyota Bharat's homepage publishes a Delhi ex-showroom price of ₹15,36,000 for the Innova Crysta. The showroom page lists both a diesel and a petrol engine and does not say which one that starting price buys.

Toyota Bharat's homepage publishes a Delhi ex-showroom price of ₹26,20,000 for the Fortuner. Petrol and diesel are both listed, and the page does not tie that starting price to one of them. Seating is 7 and the fuel tank is 80 litres on both.
The Camry Hybrid is the only powertrain on the page. Delhi ex-showroom price is ₹37,22,300. Combined hybrid output is 230 PS, engine torque is 221 Nm, and the stated fuel efficiency is 25.49 km/l.

The 2026 City starts at ₹11,99,900 ex-showroom, New Delhi. Petrol SV is the lowest grade and is offered as a 6-speed manual. That petrol engine is 1,498 cc, 121 PS and 145 Nm, with a stated 17.77 km/l.

The Amaze starts from ₹7,65,400 ex-showroom. The 1.2L i-VTEC petrol manual is the lower of the two stated mileage figures, at 18.65 km/l. The engine is 1,199 cc, 90 hp and 110 Nm. V is the first listed grade.
The 2026 Elevate starts from ₹11,80,000 ex-showroom. The manual is the lower mileage figure, 15.31 km/l. The petrol engine is 1,498 cc, 121 PS and 145 Nm.
The Slavia page says the ex-showroom price starts at ₹9,99,900. Classic is the entry trim and is offered only with the 1.0 TSI manual: 999 cc, 115 PS, 178 Nm, and 20.32 kmpl under rule 115 of CMVR.
Kia offers the Carnival Limousine+ 2026 at ₹59,64,900 ex-showroom, all India. The listed engine is a 2,151 cc diesel with 193 PS and 45 kgf.m, an 8-speed automatic, and 7 seats.
Volkswagen states an ex-showroom price of ₹10,70,900. The brochure's first 1.0 TSI column is the 6-speed manual: 999 cc, 115 PS, 178 Nm, and 20.08 km/l under rule 115 of CMVR.
Volkswagen states the new Taigun's ex-showroom price is ₹10,99,900. The brochure's first 1.0 TSI column is the 6-speed manual: 999 cc, 115 PS, 178 Nm, and 19.87 km/l under rule 115 of CMVR.

The Exter price page lists an ex-showroom start of ₹5,80,600. The specification page lists a 1.2 l Kappa petrol and a bi-fuel petrol with CNG, both 1,197 cc, five seats, 185 mm ground clearance, and a 37 litre petrol tank.
The Aura price page says the ex-showroom price starts at ₹5,99,990. The page’s short description also rounds that start to ₹5.99 lakh.
The Bayon price page lists a starting price of ₹9,99,900 ex-showroom. Every variant uses the 1.5 l MPi petrol. HX 2, the first trim, is manual.

The Alcazar price page lists a starting ex-showroom price of ₹14,50,700. The same page offers petrol and diesel, manual and automatic, and both 6-seat and 7-seat layouts, so those are not pinned to the starting car. The specification schema gives model year 2024.
The Grand i10 Nios price page says it starts at ₹5,59,700 ex-showroom. A shorter description on the same page says ₹5.55 lakh; the rupee figure in the body was used.
The i20 N Line price page lists a starting ex-showroom price of ₹9,27,200.
The Creta N Line price page says the starting ex-showroom price is ₹19,03,300. A schema offer on the same page says ₹17,83,000; the visible sentence was used.

The Venue N Line price page lists a starting price of ₹10,66,100. The specification schema gives a 998 cc engine, five seats, and model year 2025. A schema offer on the price page also says ₹10,65,400; the visible starting price was used.
The Creta Electric price page lists an ex-showroom start of ₹18,02,800. It is offered with 42 kWh and 51.4 kWh batteries, and the page does not say which pack is the starting car.
The XUV 3XO page shows an ex-showroom range starting at ₹7.79 lakh. Several petrol, CNG, and diesel engines are listed, so the starting car’s engine is not singled out.
The XUV 7XO page schema lists a low price of ₹13,99,000, matching the ex-showroom range that starts at ₹13.99 lakh. Petrol and diesel engines are both listed.
The Thar Roxx page shows an ex-showroom range starting at ₹12.52 lakh. Petrol and diesel engines are both listed.
The Scorpio Classic page schema low price is ₹13,43,200, shown on the model list as ₹13.43 lakh ex-showroom. The listed engine is the GEN-2 mHawk diesel, 97 kW (132 PS) and 300 Nm.
The Bolero Neo page lists an ex-showroom start of ₹9.06 lakh. The engine on the page is the mHawk100 diesel, 1,493 cc, 73.5 kW and 260 Nm.
The Bolero Neo+ page schema lists a low price of ₹11,46,000, matching the ex-showroom range that starts at ₹11.46 lakh.
The XUV 3XO EV list shows an ex-showroom start of ₹13.89 lakh. The page gives one battery, 39.4 kWh, with 110 kW (150 PS), 310 Nm, and 0-100 km/h in 8.3 seconds.
The Victoris price page says the ex-showroom price starts at ₹10.49 lakh. The model page lists several mileage figures and does not tie one of them to that starting car.
The Nexa Fronx page says prices start from ₹6.85 lakh. The same site states that its prices are ex-showroom prices.
The Nexa Grand Vitara page says prices start at ₹10.76 lakh. The same site states that its prices are ex-showroom prices.
The Nexa Invicto page says the price starts from ₹24.97 lakh. The same site states that its prices are ex-showroom prices.
The Nexa Jimny page says the price starts from ₹12.32 lakh. The same site states that its prices are ex-showroom prices.
The Nexa XL6 page says the price starts from ₹11.52 lakh ex-showroom.

The Octavia RS page says the ex-showroom price starts at ₹56.69 lakh. It is the 2.0 TSI petrol with 195 kW and 370 Nm, a 7-speed DSG, 0-100 km/h in 6.4 seconds, and an electronically limited top speed of 250 km/h.

The ZR-V page says the price starts from ₹49,99,900 ex-showroom in Delhi. It is the 2.0 l e:HEV hybrid, 1,993 cc, 184 PS and 315 Nm, with an e-CVT, five seats, and 22.8 km/l. The fuel tank is described as still to be announced.
The Tayron page says the ex-showroom price of Tayron Life, the starting grade, is ₹41,99,000. Tayron R-Line starts higher, at ₹47,74,000.
The Golf GTI page lists an ex-showroom price of ₹50,90,900 and says the car is currently sold out.
The Astor page says the price starts at ₹9.79 lakh, and the page schema low price is ₹9,79,000. The page tells readers that ex-showroom prices can vary by region.

The Majestor page says it starts at ₹43.49 lakh, matching the schema low price of ₹43,49,000. The listed engine is a 2.0 l twin-turbo diesel with 215.5 PS. The page tells readers that ex-showroom prices can vary by region.
The Toyota India homepage Delhi ex-showroom list gives the Innova Touring Sport at ₹19,23,000, separate from the Innova Crysta at ₹15,36,000.
